finding.claim: The unvalidated `icon` URL supplied via PUT /profile is stored and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync job with a GET request, enabling blind SSRF to internal or metadata endpoints.
finding.source: `icon` parameter of update(String webhook, String icon) (src/Profile.java:11), stored unchecked at src/Profile.java:16 via `this.iconUrl = icon;`

trace.note: Comment identifies the entry point as PUT /profile; route handler not present in this repo
Regex check applies only to `webhook`, not `icon`
`icon` stored into this.iconUrl with no validation
sync() calls URI.create(iconUrl) and issues a server-side GET
Response body read into memory via ofByteArray() but not returned to the attacker (blind)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, or allowlist check on icon; no private/loopback/link-local IP blocklist; no DNS pinning at connect time. java.net.http.HttpClient only accepts http/https, which limits schemes but does not prevent SSRF. Redirect behavior depends on the injected HttpClient (c), which is not configured in this file; default is Redirect.NEVER but unverified here. The webhook regex at line 12 is a full-string match with fixed host hooks.example.com and was checked and not reported.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check in update() is the anchored webhook regex at src/Profile.java:12, which applies to `webhook` only. `icon` is stored unchecked at src/Profile.java:16 and passed to URI.create(iconUrl) and a GET at src/Profile.java:23-24 with no scheme, host, or private-address check.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (comment at line 10, icon parameter at line 11, regex at line 12 covering webhook only, store at line 16, server-side GET at lines 23-24 with the body discarded), and no closing guard exists in src/Profile.java. The caveat is that the PUT /profile route handler, its authentication, and the injected HttpClient's redirect policy are not in this repo, so the claim that a low-privilege user can reach this with an `icon` value rests on the comment at line 10 rather than on code I could read.
